newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo naphtha little changed in slow trading.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo naphtha little changed in slow trading.

text.p: Tokyo naphtha prices were virtually unchanged in slim afternoon talks on Friday, traders said.
Trading is expected to get back into full swing next Tuesday after the three-day weekend in Japan, they added.
Open-spec naphtha second-half July was assessed at $209.00/210.00 per tonne. It was sold at $210.00 on Thursday.
In inter-month spreads, first-half August was valued 25 to 50 cents above first-half July. Ample supplies are weighing heavily on nearby months.
Earlier this week, the one-month spread from first-half July was assessed at plus $1.00/1.25.

In middle distillates, activity has been subdued since two Japanese oil firms each procured one jet cargo from South Korea last week at $1.10 and $1.30 per tonne over the mean of Singapore quotes, respectively.
Gas oil trading, which usually picks up toward the summer driving season, remained quiet due to ample domestic stocks.
Spot cargoes of low sulphur waxy residue (LSWR) were assessed at parity to 30 cents per barrel over the Pertamina formula, fuel oil traders said.
